# Bugs — `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`

No code bugs were found in this module. All scope functions admit correct
specs as written; the only obstacles are a Verus language limitation and a
deferred abstraction, both recorded below for the proving phase.

## Not a code bug — Verus limitation (int-to-ptr cast)

`Table::read` / `Table::write` materialize a raw pointer from the integer base
address (`usize as *const/*mut PteWord`) and perform a volatile access of
externally-owned page-table memory. Verus does not support `usize`→pointer
casts (`error: Verus does not support this cast: usize to *const u32`). This is
a tooling limitation, not a logic error in the code. Mitigated with the
documented `external_body` trust boundary (see `verus-unsupported.md` and
`verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`). No fix required.

## Resolved (Turn 1 review) — read/write now carry full contracts

The earlier "deferred round-trip / addr-only View" note was resolved during the
Turn 1 specification review. `read`/`write` and the `TableEntry` codec now carry
complete `#[verus_spec]` contracts referencing a **global, parameter-free**
page-table-memory ghost (`spec_table_word`/`spec_table_read`), mirroring
`frame::instance`→`phys_view()`. No exec signature changed, so the out-of-scope
`admit()` callers do not cascade (`make verify`: kernel 76 verified, 0 errors).
The `entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>` model and the read-after-write round-trip law
(`lemma_entry_roundtrip`) are now expressed, not deferred. `read`/`write` remain
`external_body` only for the genuine Verus `usize`→pointer limitation below.

===bugs.md===
# Bugs — `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`

No code bugs were found in this module. All scope functions admit correct
specs as written; the only obstacles are a Verus language limitation and a
deferred abstraction, both recorded below for the proving phase.

## Not a code bug — Verus limitation (int-to-ptr cast)

`Table::read` / `Table::write` materialize a raw pointer from the integer base
address (`usize as *const/*mut PteWord`) and perform a volatile access of
externally-owned page-table memory. Verus does not support `usize`→pointer
casts (`error: Verus does not support this cast: usize to *const u32`). This is
a tooling limitation, not a logic error in the code. Mitigated with the
documented `external_body` trust boundary (see `verus-unsupported.md` and
`verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`). No fix required.

## Resolved (Turn 1 review) — read/write now carry full contracts

The earlier "deferred round-trip / addr-only View" note was resolved during the
Turn 1 specification review. `read`/`write` and the `TableEntry` codec now carry
complete `#[verus_spec]` contracts referencing a **global, parameter-free**
page-table-memory ghost (`spec_table_word`/`spec_table_read`), mirroring
`frame::instance`→`phys_view()`. No exec signature changed, so the out-of-scope
`admit()` callers do not cascade (`make verify`: kernel 76 verified, 0 errors).
The `entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>` model and the read-after-write round-trip law
(`lemma_entry_roundtrip`) are now expressed, not deferred. `read`/`write` remain
`external_body` only for the genuine Verus `usize`→pointer limitation below.

Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.

## Allowed `external_body`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::instance` — materializes a `&'static mut Inner` from the

  Raw-memory op over externally-owned `static mut` storage Verus cannot verify without a

  state to `phys_view().frames`, asserts `(*r).inv()`, and records `phys_view().initialized` —
  the §8 ghost-token attachment for the singleton frame allocator.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`

  `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory

154. #[derive(Debug)]
155. pub struct Table<E: TableEntry> {
156.     /// Base address of the table (must be page-aligned).
157.     base: usize,
158.     /// Phantom marker for the entry type.
159.     _marker: ::core::marker::PhantomData<E>,
160. }
161. 
162. #[verus_verify]
163. impl<E: TableEntry> Table<E> {
164.     ///
165.     /// # Description
166.     ///
167.     /// Creates a table reference from a base address.
168.     ///
169.     /// # Safety
170.     ///
171.     /// `base` must be a valid, page-aligned address with at least one page of readable/writable
172.     /// memory.
173.     ///
174.     #[verus_spec(result =>
175.         ensures result@.addr == base as nat,
176.     )]
177.     pub const unsafe fn from_address(base: usize) -> Self {
178.         Self {
179.             base,
180.             _marker: ::core::marker::PhantomData,
181.         }
182.     }
183. 
184.     ///
185.     /// # Description
186.     ///
187.     /// Reads the entry at `index`.
188.     ///
189.     /// Returns `None` if the raw value is invalid according to `E::from_raw()`.
190.     ///
191.     /// # Safety
192.     ///
193.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile read.
194.     ///
195.     // Trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/.../tcb-allowed.md` and `verus-unsupported.md`):
196.     // materializes a raw `*const PteWord` from the integer base address (`usize as *const`) and
197.     // performs a volatile load — the hardware page-table access. Verus does not support the
198.     // `usize -> *const T` cast, so the body cannot be verified; this mirrors the
199.     // `bump_allocator::alloc` / `frame::instance` int-to-pointer materialization boundaries.
200.     // The `ensures` pins the (trusted) result to the global page-table memory ghost, exactly as
201.     // `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` — no exec signature change.
202.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
203.     #[verus_spec(result =>
204.         requires
205.             index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
206.         ensures
207.             result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@),
208.     )]
209.     pub unsafe fn read(&self, index: TableIndex) -> Option<E> {
210.         let offset: usize = index.into_raw() << PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2;
211.         let ptr: *const PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *const PteWord;
212.         E::from_raw(::core::ptr::read_volatile(ptr))
213.     }
214. 
215.     ///
216.     /// # Description
217.     ///
218.     /// Writes `entry` at `index`.
219.     ///
220.     /// # Safety
221.     ///
222.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile write.
223.     ///
224.     // Trust boundary (see `tcb-allowed.md` / `verus-unsupported.md`): materializes a raw
225.     // `*mut PteWord` from the integer base address and performs a volatile store — the hardware
226.     // page-table write. The `usize -> *mut T` cast is unsupported by Verus, so the body cannot be
227.     // verified; same int-to-pointer boundary as `read`.
228.     //
229.     // No contents `ensures`: page-table memory is *mutable* volatile state, but `write` takes
230.     // `&self` and the global ghost `spec_table_word(addr, index)` is a *pure* function (one fixed
231.     // value per slot). Pinning that pure cell to the caller-chosen `entry` in an `external_body`
232.     // (hence *assumed*) postcondition is unsound — two writes of distinct entries to the same slot
233.     // would assume `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, and with `lemma_entry_roundtrip`
234.     // that derives `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false`. The slot-update transition
235.     // (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)` after the call, with all other slots framed) is a
236.     // genuine `old@ -> @` state change and is therefore *deferred to the proving-phase page-table
237.     // permission token* — exactly the deferral convention used by `identity_map_view()`'s
238.     // `v -> v'` in `identity_map.spec.rs` (a global accessor whose cross-call transition is
239.     // realized later by a ghost token, "not a verification escape"). Only the sound `requires`
240.     // (in-range index, auto from `TableIndex::inv`) is kept here.
241.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
242.     #[verus_spec(
243.         requires
244.             index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
245.     )]
246.     pub unsafe fn write(&self, index: TableIndex, entry: E) {
247.         let offset: usize = index.into_raw() << PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2;
248.         let ptr: *mut PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *mut PteWord;
249.         ::core::ptr::write_volatile(ptr, entry.raw());
250.     }
251. }
252.

1. verus! {
2. 
3. //==================================================================================================
4. // TableIndex — a validated page-table slot number
5. //==================================================================================================
6. 
7. // A `TableIndex` carries exactly one piece of caller-visible information: the validated index
8. // value. Its abstract value is a single `nat` (see `view_design.md`).
9. impl View for TableIndex {
10.     type V = nat;
11. 
12.     // `closed`: callers reference `self@` and the in-range invariant; the mapping to the inner
13.     // `usize` field is hidden. The abstract value is "the validated slot number".
14.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> nat {
15.         self.0 as nat
16.     }
17. }
18. 
19. impl TableIndex {
20.     // The validated-range guarantee every caller depends on: a `TableIndex` is always a legal
21.     // slot. Enforced as a type invariant so the bound holds unconditionally for any value callers
22.     // hold — this is exactly what keeps `read`/`write` (and `gva.rs`'s `checked_mul`) within one
23.     // page, and is established once at each construction site (`new`, `pd_index`, `pt_index`).
24.     #[verifier::type_invariant]
25.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
26.         self@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH
27.     }
28. }
29. 
30. //==================================================================================================
31. // Virtual-address index extraction (pure helpers)
32. //==================================================================================================
33. 
34. // Low `log2(PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)` bits of `vaddr >> shift`. Mirrors the exec masking
35. // `(vaddr >> shift) & (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)` exactly; the mask makes the result `< LEN`.
36. pub open spec fn spec_table_index(vaddr: usize, shift: usize) -> nat {
37.     ((vaddr >> shift) & ((crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1) as usize)) as nat
38. }
39. 
40. // PD index = bits [PGTAB_SHIFT, PGTAB_SHIFT + log2(LEN)) of `vaddr`.
41. pub open spec fn spec_pd_index(vaddr: usize) -> nat {
42.     spec_table_index(vaddr, crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT)
43. }
44. 
45. // PT index = bits [PAGE_SHIFT, PAGE_SHIFT + log2(LEN)) of `vaddr`.
46. pub open spec fn spec_pt_index(vaddr: usize) -> nat {
47.     spec_table_index(vaddr, crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT)
48. }
49. 
50. //==================================================================================================
51. // TableEntry codec (the per-entry round-trip law)
52. //==================================================================================================
53. 
54. // Abstract serialization / decoding of a `TableEntry`. These mirror the exec `raw` / `from_raw`
55. // trait methods. They are deliberately *unbounded* over `E` (no `TableEntry` bound) to avoid a
56. // definitional cycle (`TableEntry`'s method specs reference these, so a bound here would make the
57. // trait depend on a function that depends on the trait).
58. //
59. // `spec_entry_from_raw` returns `None` for a word that is not a valid encoding of `E` — exactly
60. // the `read` failure path callers map to `InvalidArgument` (see `caller_analysis.md`).
61. pub uninterp spec fn spec_entry_raw<E>(e: E) -> PteWord;
62. 
63. pub uninterp spec fn spec_entry_from_raw<E>(w: PteWord) -> Option<E>;
64. 
65. //==================================================================================================
66. // Global ghost model of page-table memory
67. //==================================================================================================
68. 
69. // Page-table memory is volatile, caller-owned storage the `Table<E>` handle does not contain
70. // (the struct holds only `base`). It is modeled here as a *global, parameter-free* ghost
71. // function — the same device used for the physical-frame subsystem (`mm::phys::phys_view()`):
72. // the abstract state is named globally rather than threaded through a permission parameter, so
73. // `read`/`write` keep their exec signatures and do not cascade ghost arguments into out-of-scope
74. // callers (`identity_map::ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page`).
75. //
76. // `spec_table_word(addr, index)` is the raw word currently stored at slot `index` of the
77. // page-table page based at `addr`. Because it is a pure function, a call to `write` only updates
78. // knowledge about the *one* slot named in its `ensures`; every other slot/page is automatically
79. // preserved across the call (the caller-facing frame condition). The cross-call write transition
80. // (and its consistency when the same slot is written twice) is realized in the proving phase by a
81. // ghost token over the page-table pages — exactly the `phys_view()` "transition realized in the
82. // proving phase" placeholder.
83. pub uninterp spec fn spec_table_word(addr: nat, index: nat) -> PteWord;
84. 
85. // The decoded entry currently stored at slot `index` of the page based at `addr`: the value a
86. // `read` returns. This is the `index -> Option<E>` entry map from `view_design.md`, expressed
87. // pointwise over the global word store.
88. pub open spec fn spec_table_read<E>(addr: nat, index: nat) -> Option<E> {
89.     spec_entry_from_raw::<E>(spec_table_word(addr, index))
90. }
91. 
92. //==================================================================================================
93. // Table<E> — a typed, non-owning handle over one page-table page
94. //==================================================================================================
95. 
96. // To callers a `Table<E>` is a typed handle over the page at a physical/identity-mapped base
97. // address (see `view_design.md`): its caller-meaningful identity is *which page* read/write act
98. // on (`addr`), and its observable contents are the per-slot decoded entry map (`entries`). The
99. // contents live in volatile, caller-owned memory the struct does not store, so the view reads
100. // them from the global `spec_table_read` ghost rather than from struct fields.
101. pub struct TableView<E> {
102.     /// Physical/identity-mapped base address this handle denotes.
103.     pub addr: nat,
104.     /// Decoded entry at each valid slot — `entries[i]` is what `read(i)` returns
105.     /// (`None` = the slot holds a word that is not a valid encoding of `E`).
106.     pub entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>,
107. }
108. 
109. impl<E: TableEntry> View for Table<E> {
110.     type V = TableView<E>;
111. 
112.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> TableView<E> {
113.         TableView {
114.             addr: self.base as nat,
115.             entries: Map::new(
116.                 |i: nat| i < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
117.                 |i: nat| spec_table_read::<E>(self.base as nat, i),
118.             ),
119.         }
120.     }
121. }
122. 
123. } // verus!
124.

1. # Caller Analysis: `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`
2. 
3. ## Script Output
4. 
5. Raw `find_callers_lsp.py` output reported **7 public exec functions, 0 private,
6. 2 types (`Table`, `TableIndex`)** and — importantly — **0 external callers for
7. every public function** (only internal callers of `TableIndex::into_raw` from
8. `Table::read`/`Table::write`).
9. 
10. > **Why the script found 0 external callers (false negative).**
11. > This module lives under `src/libs/arch/src/x86/` — the **32-bit x86** build.
12. > rust-analyzer (and thus the script) indexes the **x86_64 host** configuration,
13. > so all real call sites — which are compiled only under `cfg(target_arch =
14. > "x86")` (kernel) or are host-side software page-walkers — are invisible to the
15. > LSP. A textual search across the workspace recovers the true callers below.
16. > Treat the script's "no external callers" warning as a configuration artifact,
17. > **not** as evidence of dead code.
18. 
19. In-scope (verification-order) functions: `Table::write`, `TableIndex::into_raw`,
20. `raw`, `Table::read`, `from_raw`, `pt_index`, `TableIndex`, `pd_index`,
21. `Table::from_address`. (`raw`/`from_raw` are the `TableEntry` trait methods,
22. implemented in `pde.rs`/`pte.rs` and dispatched only inside `Table::read`/`write`.)
23. 
24. ## Real Callers (recovered by source search)
25. 
26. ### 1. Kernel identity map — `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs` (primary consumer)
27. 
28. This is the canonical user of the whole module. It walks/builds the kernel's
29. two-level identity map:
30. 
31. - `paging::pd_index(vaddr)` / `paging::pt_index(vaddr)` → `TableIndex`
32.   (L131, L306, L728, L729, L783, L848).
33. - `unsafe { Table::<PageDirectoryEntry>::from_address(pd_paddr) }` and
34.   `Table::<PageTableEntry>::from_address(pt_paddr)` to obtain a typed view over a
35.   physical (identity-mapped) page (L133, L297, L299, L732, L736, L785, L852, L863).
36. - `unsafe { pd.read(pde_idx) }` / `pt.read(pte_idx)` returning
37.   `Option<PageDirectoryEntry>` / `Option<PageTableEntry>`; callers treat `None`
38.   as "invalid entry" → `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` (L308, L316, L535, L633,
39.   L786, L853, L864).
40. - `unsafe { pd.write(pde_idx, new_pde) }` / `pt.write(pte_idx, new_pte)` to
41.   install freshly-built entries (L320, L583, L665).
42. - The entry-type parameter `E` is fixed per level: PD tables only carry
43.   `PageDirectoryEntry`, PT tables only `PageTableEntry`. The phantom-typed
44.   `Table<E>` is exactly what enforces this at the call sites.
45. 
46. ### 2. UserVM guest page walker — `src/uservm/src/guest_profiler/gva.rs` (host-side)
47. 
48. `translate_gva()` performs a *software* two-level walk over guest memory:
49. 
50. ```rust
51. let pd_index: usize = paging::pd_index(gva as usize).into_raw();
52. let pt_index: usize = paging::pt_index(gva as usize).into_raw();
53. ```
54. 
55. Here only `pd_index`/`pt_index` and `TableIndex::into_raw` are used; the table
56. bytes are read directly from a host pointer (`read_unaligned`) rather than via
57. `Table::read`, because the guest's memory is not mapped into the host address
58. space. This caller relies *solely* on the index-extraction arithmetic being
59. correct (mask to `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`) and on `into_raw` returning that same
60. value unchanged.
61. 
62. ## Pre-existing Specs (from upstream verification)
63. 
64. - **Source:** added while verifying the kernel `mm::virt::identity_map` module.
65. - **File:** `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs`.
66. - These are **trusted external boundary specs** for this not-yet-verified module:
67.   - `#[verifier::external_type_specification] #[external_body]` for
68.     `Table<E>` (`ExTable`) and `TableIndex` (`ExTableIndex`) — both opaque.
69.   - `#[verifier::external_trait_specification]` for `TableEntry` (`ExTableEntry`,
70.     `: Copy`).
71.   - `assume_specification` (no `requires`/`ensures` — state-free placeholders) for
72.     `pd_index`, `pt_index`, `Table::<E>::from_address`, `Table::<E>::read`,
73.     `Table::<E>::write`, plus `invlpg`.
74. - Functions WITHOUT specs: `TableIndex::new`, `TableIndex::into_raw`,
75.   and the `TableEntry::raw`/`from_raw` trait methods (no external spec; opaque).
76. - View type: **none** — `Table`/`TableIndex` are currently opaque (`external_body`).
77. 
78. ### Assessment
79. 
80. - **Coverage:** partial. Only the functions the identity-map walker needed are
81.   given boundary specs; `into_raw`/`new` and the `raw`/`from_raw` trait methods
82.   are unspecified.
83. - **Strength:** weak — the `assume_specification`s are state-free with no
84.   `ensures`, and the corresponding obligations in the exec bodies are
85.   `admit()`-ed (`ensure_pte`, `ensure_pt`, etc.). They exist only to let the
86.   identity-map bodies translate, not to prove anything about table contents.
87. - **View design:** absent / biased. There is no abstract `View` yet; `Table` is
88.   fully opaque. A real View must model a table as a finite map
89.   `TableIndex → Option<E>` so that `read` after `write` can be reasoned about —
90.   the current opaque placeholder cannot express the read/write round-trip the
91.   identity map relies on.
92. 
93. ## Trait Obligations
94. 
95. - **Trait `TableEntry: Copy`** — semantics expected by `Table`:
96.   - `from_raw(raw) -> Option<Self>`: parse a raw `PteWord` (`u32`), returning
97.     `None` exactly for raw values that are not a valid encoding of `E`.
98.   - `raw(self) -> PteWord`: serialize back to the raw word.
99.   - Round-trip expectation from callers: an entry built via `E::new(...)` and
100.     written, then read back, must yield `Some(equivalent entry)`; an
101.     all-zero / not-present word read by the identity map is a *valid* entry
102.     (returns `Some`, with `is_present() == false`) — `None` denotes structural
103.     corruption, which callers surface as `InvalidArgument`.
104.   - `Copy` lets `write` take `entry` by value and `read` return it freely.
105. 
106. ## Caller Expectations
107. 
108. ### `pd_index(vaddr) -> TableIndex`
109. - Callers assume: returns the PD index = `(vaddr >> PGTAB_SHIFT) &
110.   (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)`, always in `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`. Total (no panic,
111.   no failure) for any `usize`. `const`.
112. - Callers don't care about: how the bits are masked, or that the result wraps an
113.   internal `usize` — only that `into_raw()` of it equals the masked value.
114. 
115. ### `pt_index(vaddr) -> TableIndex`
116. - Callers assume: returns the PT index = `(vaddr >> PAGE_SHIFT) &
117.   (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)`, always in range; total; `const`.
118. - Callers don't care about: internal representation.
119. 
120. ### `TableIndex` (type) / `TableIndex::into_raw(self) -> usize`
121. - Callers assume: a `TableIndex` is a *validated* index, guaranteed
122.   `< PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`; `into_raw` is the identity projection back to that
123.   validated `usize` (loss-less, total, `const`). `gva.rs` multiplies it by entry
124.   size with `checked_mul`, relying on the bound to stay within a page.
125. - Callers don't care about: that it is a newtype over `usize`; only the in-range
126.   invariant and the round-trip with the index extractors matter.
127. 
128. ### `Table::from_address(base) -> Table<E>` (`unsafe`, `const`)
129. - Callers assume: produces a typed, non-owning handle over the page at physical/
130.   identity-mapped `base`; cheap, infallible, side-effect-free. The caller carries
131.   the safety obligation (`base` page-aligned, mapped, readable/writable).
132. - Callers don't care about: that the struct stores only `base` + a `PhantomData`
133.   marker; they care that the phantom type `E` is threaded so PD/PT handles can't
134.   be confused.
135. 
136. ### `Table::read(&self, index) -> Option<E>` (`unsafe`)
137. - Callers assume: volatile-reads the word at `base + index*4` and decodes it via
138.   `E::from_raw`; `Some(e)` for a valid encoding, `None` for an invalid one. Does
139.   not mutate the table. The validated `index` guarantees in-bounds access.
140. - Callers don't care about: the volatile-read mechanism or the `<<
141.   PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2` offset math — only the index→entry mapping and the `None`
142.   = "invalid entry" contract (which they map to `InvalidArgument`).
143. 
144. ### `Table::write(&self, index, entry)` (`unsafe`)
145. - Callers assume: volatile-writes `entry.raw()` to `base + index*4`, so that a
146.   subsequent `read(index)` observes `Some(entry)` (read-after-write round-trip).
147.   Only the targeted slot changes. The validated `index` keeps the write in
148.   bounds of the page.
149. - Callers don't care about: the volatile mechanism or offset computation.
150. 
151. ### `TableEntry::from_raw` / `TableEntry::raw`
152. - No direct external callers; invoked only inside `read`/`write`. Expectation is
153.   the round-trip described under *Trait Obligations*.
154. 
155. ## Abstract Resource
156. 
157. This module manages a **single hardware page-table page** as a fixed-length array
158. of `PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` typed entries, addressed by a *validated* in-range index
159. (`TableIndex`) and accessed by raw base address. Abstractly it is a partial map
160. `TableIndex → Option<E>` over volatile memory the caller owns, plus the pure
161. helpers that derive the PD/PT index of a virtual address.
162. 
163. ## Key Invariants (caller perspective)
164. 
165. - **Index validity:** every `TableIndex` (whether from `pd_index`, `pt_index`, or
166.   `new`) satisfies `into_raw() < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`; this bound is what keeps
167.   `read`/`write` (and `gva.rs`'s `checked_mul`) within one page.
168. - **Index extraction correctness:** `pd_index`/`pt_index` return exactly the
169.   masked/shifted bit-field of `vaddr`, and `into_raw` returns that same value.
170. - **Read/write round-trip:** `write(i, e)` followed by `read(i)` yields
171.   `Some(e')` with `e'` decoding-equivalent to `e`; writes touch only slot `i`.
172. - **Decode totality:** `read` returns `None` only for raw words that are not a
173.   valid `E` encoding; a not-present (zeroed) entry is a valid `Some`, not `None`.
174. - **Type discipline:** `Table<E>`'s phantom `E` prevents mixing PD and PT entries
175.   across table levels — a property callers depend on but that has no runtime cost.
176. - **Non-ownership:** `from_address` does not allocate or free; lifetime/validity
177.   of the backing page is the caller's responsibility (encoded as `unsafe`).
178.

     `pd_index`, `pt_index`, `Table::<E>::from_address`, `Table::<E>::read`,
     `Table::<E>::write`, plus `invlpg`.

   and the `TableEntry::raw`/`from_raw` trait methods (no external spec; opaque).

 - **Coverage:** partial. Only the functions the identity-map walker needed are
   given boundary specs; `into_raw`/`new` and the `raw`/`from_raw` trait methods
   are unspecified.
 - **Strength:** weak — the `assume_specification`s are state-free with no
   `ensures`, and the corresponding obligations in the exec bodies are
   `admit()`-ed (`ensure_pte`, `ensure_pt`, etc.). They exist only to let the
   identity-map bodies translate, not to prove anything about table contents.
 - **View design:** absent / biased. There is no abstract `View` yet; `Table` is
   fully opaque. A real View must model a table as a finite map
   `TableIndex → Option<E>` so that `read` after `write` can be reasoned about —
   the current opaque placeholder cannot express the read/write round-trip the
   identity map relies on.
 
 ## Trait Obligations
 
 - **Trait `TableEntry: Copy`** — semantics expected by `Table`:
   - `from_raw(raw) -> Option<Self>`: parse a raw `PteWord` (`u32`), returning
     `None` exactly for raw values that are not a valid encoding of `E`.
   - `raw(self) -> PteWord`: serialize back to the raw word.
   - Round-trip expectation from callers: an entry built via `E::new(...)` and
     written, then read back, must yield `Some(equivalent entry)`; an
     all-zero / not-present word read by the identity map is a *valid* entry
     (returns `Some`, with `is_present() == false`) — `None` denotes structural
     corruption, which callers surface as `InvalidArgument`.
   - `Copy` lets `write` take `entry` by value and `read` return it freely.
 
 ## Caller Expectations
 
 ### `pd_index(vaddr) -> TableIndex`
 - Callers assume: returns the PD index = `(vaddr >> PGTAB_SHIFT) &
   (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)`, always in `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`. Total (no panic,
   no failure) for any `usize`. `const`.
 - Callers don't care about: how the bits are masked, or that the result wraps an
   internal `usize` — only that `into_raw()` of it equals the masked value.
 
 ### `pt_index(vaddr) -> TableIndex`
 - Callers assume: returns the PT index = `(vaddr >> PAGE_SHIFT) &
   (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)`, always in range; total; `const`.
 - Callers don't care about: internal representation.
 
 ### `TableIndex` (type) / `TableIndex::into_raw(self) -> usize`
 - Callers assume: a `TableIndex` is a *validated* index, guaranteed
   `< PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`; `into_raw` is the identity projection back to that
   validated `usize` (loss-less, total, `const`). `gva.rs` multiplies it by entry
   size with `checked_mul`, relying on the bound to stay within a page.
 - Callers don't care about: that it is a newtype over `usize`; only the in-range
   invariant and the round-trip with the index extractors matter.
 
 ### `Table::from_address(base) -> Table<E>` (`unsafe`, `const`)
 - Callers assume: produces a typed, non-owning handle over the page at physical/
   identity-mapped `base`; cheap, infallible, side-effect-free. The caller carries
   the safety obligation (`base` page-aligned, mapped, readable/writable).
 - Callers don't care about: that the struct stores only `base` + a `PhantomData`
   marker; they care that the phantom type `E` is threaded so PD/PT handles can't
   be confused.
 
 ### `Table::read(&self, index) -> Option<E>` (`unsafe`)
 - Callers assume: volatile-reads the word at `base + index*4` and decodes it via
   `E::from_raw`; `Some(e)` for a valid encoding, `None` for an invalid one. Does
   not mutate the table. The validated `index` guarantees in-bounds access.
 - Callers don't care about: the volatile-read mechanism or the `<<
   PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2` offset math — only the index→entry mapping and the `None`
   = "invalid entry" contract (which they map to `InvalidArgument`).
 
 ### `Table::write(&self, index, entry)` (`unsafe`)
 - Callers assume: volatile-writes `entry.raw()` to `base + index*4`, so that a
   subsequent `read(index)` observes `Some(entry)` (read-after-write round-trip).
   Only the targeted slot changes. The validated `index` keeps the write in
   bounds of the page.
 - Callers don't care about: the volatile mechanism or offset computation.
 
 ### `TableEntry::from_raw` / `TableEntry::raw`
 - No direct external callers; invoked only inside `read`/`write`. Expectation is
   the round-trip described under *Trait Obligations*.
 
 ## Abstract Resource
 
 This module manages a **single hardware page-table page** as a fixed-length array
 of `PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` typed entries, addressed by a *validated* in-range index
 (`TableIndex`) and accessed by raw base address. Abstractly it is a partial map
 `TableIndex → Option<E>` over volatile memory the caller owns, plus the pure
 helpers that derive the PD/PT index of a virtual address.
 
 ## Key Invariants (caller perspective)
 
 - **Index validity:** every `TableIndex` (whether from `pd_index`, `pt_index`, or
   `new`) satisfies `into_raw() < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`; this bound is what keeps
   `read`/`write` (and `gva.rs`'s `checked_mul`) within one page.
 - **Index extraction correctness:** `pd_index`/`pt_index` return exactly the
   masked/shifted bit-field of `vaddr`, and `into_raw` returns that same value.
 - **Read/write round-trip:** `write(i, e)` followed by `read(i)` yields
   `Some(e')` with `e'` decoding-equivalent to `e`; writes touch only slot `i`.
 - **Decode totality:** `read` returns `None` only for raw words that are not a
   valid `E` encoding; a not-present (zeroed) entry is a valid `Some`, not `None`.
 - **Type discipline:** `Table<E>`'s phantom `E` prevents mixing PD and PT entries
   across table levels — a property callers depend on but that has no runtime cost.
 - **Non-ownership:** `from_address` does not allocate or free; lifetime/validity
   of the backing page is the caller's responsibility (encoded as `unsafe`).

3. //==================================================================================================
4. // TableIndex — a validated page-table slot number
5. //==================================================================================================
6. 
7. // A `TableIndex` carries exactly one piece of caller-visible information: the validated index
8. // value. Its abstract value is a single `nat` (see `view_design.md`).
9. impl View for TableIndex {
10.     type V = nat;
11. 
12.     // `closed`: callers reference `self@` and the in-range invariant; the mapping to the inner
13.     // `usize` field is hidden. The abstract value is "the validated slot number".
14.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> nat {
15.         self.0 as nat
16.     }
17. }
18. 
19. impl TableIndex {
20.     // The validated-range guarantee every caller depends on: a `TableIndex` is always a legal
21.     // slot. Enforced as a type invariant so the bound holds unconditionally for any value callers
22.     // hold — this is exactly what keeps `read`/`write` (and `gva.rs`'s `checked_mul`) within one
23.     // page, and is established once at each construction site (`new`, `pd_index`, `pt_index`).
24.     #[verifier::type_invariant]
25.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
26.         self@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH
27.     }
28. }
29. 
30. //==================================================================================================
31. // Virtual-address index extraction (pure helpers)
32. //==================================================================================================
33. 
34. // Low `log2(PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)` bits of `vaddr >> shift`. Mirrors the exec masking
35. // `(vaddr >> shift) & (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)` exactly; the mask makes the result `< LEN`.
36. pub open spec fn spec_table_index(vaddr: usize, shift: usize) -> nat {
37.     ((vaddr >> shift) & ((crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1) as usize)) as nat
38. }
39. 
40. // PD index = bits [PGTAB_SHIFT, PGTAB_SHIFT + log2(LEN)) of `vaddr`.
41. pub open spec fn spec_pd_index(vaddr: usize) -> nat {
42.     spec_table_index(vaddr, crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT)
43. }
44. 
45. // PT index = bits [PAGE_SHIFT, PAGE_SHIFT + log2(LEN)) of `vaddr`.
46. pub open spec fn spec_pt_index(vaddr: usize) -> nat {
47.     spec_table_index(vaddr, crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT)
48. }
49. 
50. //==================================================================================================
51. // TableEntry codec (the per-entry round-trip law)
52. //==================================================================================================
53. 
54. // Abstract serialization / decoding of a `TableEntry`. These mirror the exec `raw` / `from_raw`
55. // trait methods. They are deliberately *unbounded* over `E` (no `TableEntry` bound) to avoid a
56. // definitional cycle (`TableEntry`'s method specs reference these, so a bound here would make the
57. // trait depend on a function that depends on the trait).
58. //
59. // `spec_entry_from_raw` returns `None` for a word that is not a valid encoding of `E` — exactly
60. // the `read` failure path callers map to `InvalidArgument` (see `caller_analysis.md`).
61. pub uninterp spec fn spec_entry_raw<E>(e: E) -> PteWord;
62. 
63. pub uninterp spec fn spec_entry_from_raw<E>(w: PteWord) -> Option<E>;
64. 
65. //==================================================================================================
66. // Global ghost model of page-table memory
67. //==================================================================================================
68. 
69. // Page-table memory is volatile, caller-owned storage the `Table<E>` handle does not contain
70. // (the struct holds only `base`). It is modeled here as a *global, parameter-free* ghost
71. // function — the same device used for the physical-frame subsystem (`mm::phys::phys_view()`):
72. // the abstract state is named globally rather than threaded through a permission parameter, so
73. // `read`/`write` keep their exec signatures and do not cascade ghost arguments into out-of-scope
74. // callers (`identity_map::ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page`).
75. //
76. // `spec_table_word(addr, index)` is the raw word currently stored at slot `index` of the
77. // page-table page based at `addr`. Because it is a pure function, a call to `write` only updates
78. // knowledge about the *one* slot named in its `ensures`; every other slot/page is automatically
79. // preserved across the call (the caller-facing frame condition). The cross-call write transition
80. // (and its consistency when the same slot is written twice) is realized in the proving phase by a
81. // ghost token over the page-table pages — exactly the `phys_view()` "transition realized in the
82. // proving phase" placeholder.
83. pub uninterp spec fn spec_table_word(addr: nat, index: nat) -> PteWord;
84. 
85. // The decoded entry currently stored at slot `index` of the page based at `addr`: the value a
86. // `read` returns. This is the `index -> Option<E>` entry map from `view_design.md`, expressed
87. // pointwise over the global word store.
88. pub open spec fn spec_table_read<E>(addr: nat, index: nat) -> Option<E> {
89.     spec_entry_from_raw::<E>(spec_table_word(addr, index))
90. }
91. 
92. //==================================================================================================
93. // Table<E> — a typed, non-owning handle over one page-table page
94. //==================================================================================================
95. 
96. // To callers a `Table<E>` is a typed handle over the page at a physical/identity-mapped base
97. // address (see `view_design.md`): its caller-meaningful identity is *which page* read/write act
98. // on (`addr`), and its observable contents are the per-slot decoded entry map (`entries`). The
99. // contents live in volatile, caller-owned memory the struct does not store, so the view reads
100. // them from the global `spec_table_read` ghost rather than from struct fields.
101. pub struct TableView<E> {
102.     /// Physical/identity-mapped base address this handle denotes.
103.     pub addr: nat,
104.     /// Decoded entry at each valid slot — `entries[i]` is what `read(i)` returns
105.     /// (`None` = the slot holds a word that is not a valid encoding of `E`).
106.     pub entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>,
107. }

111.

115.             entries: Map::new(
116.                 |i: nat| i < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
117.                 |i: nat| spec_table_read::<E>(self.base as nat, i),
118.             ),
119.         }
120.     }
121. }

1. # Caller Analysis: `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`
2. 
3. ## Script Output
4. 
5. Raw `find_callers_lsp.py` output reported **7 public exec functions, 0 private,
6. 2 types (`Table`, `TableIndex`)** and — importantly — **0 external callers for
7. every public function** (only internal callers of `TableIndex::into_raw` from
8. `Table::read`/`Table::write`).
9. 
10. > **Why the script found 0 external callers (false negative).**
11. > This module lives under `src/libs/arch/src/x86/` — the **32-bit x86** build.
12. > rust-analyzer (and thus the script) indexes the **x86_64 host** configuration,
13. > so all real call sites — which are compiled only under `cfg(target_arch =
14. > "x86")` (kernel) or are host-side software page-walkers — are invisible to the
15. > LSP. A textual search across the workspace recovers the true callers below.
16. > Treat the script's "no external callers" warning as a configuration artifact,
17. > **not** as evidence of dead code.
18. 
19. In-scope (verification-order) functions: `Table::write`, `TableIndex::into_raw`,
20. `raw`, `Table::read`, `from_raw`, `pt_index`, `TableIndex`, `pd_index`,
21. `Table::from_address`. (`raw`/`from_raw` are the `TableEntry` trait methods,
22. implemented in `pde.rs`/`pte.rs` and dispatched only inside `Table::read`/`write`.)
23. 
24. ## Real Callers (recovered by source search)
25. 
26. ### 1. Kernel identity map — `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs` (primary consumer)
27. 
28. This is the canonical user of the whole module. It walks/builds the kernel's
29. two-level identity map:
30. 
31. - `paging::pd_index(vaddr)` / `paging::pt_index(vaddr)` → `TableIndex`
32.   (L131, L306, L728, L729, L783, L848).
33. - `unsafe { Table::<PageDirectoryEntry>::from_address(pd_paddr) }` and
34.   `Table::<PageTableEntry>::from_address(pt_paddr)` to obtain a typed view over a
35.   physical (identity-mapped) page (L133, L297, L299, L732, L736, L785, L852, L863).
36. - `unsafe { pd.read(pde_idx) }` / `pt.read(pte_idx)` returning
37.   `Option<PageDirectoryEntry>` / `Option<PageTableEntry>`; callers treat `None`
38.   as "invalid entry" → `ErrorCode::InvalidArgument` (L308, L316, L535, L633,
39.   L786, L853, L864).
40. - `unsafe { pd.write(pde_idx, new_pde) }` / `pt.write(pte_idx, new_pte)` to
41.   install freshly-built entries (L320, L583, L665).
42. - The entry-type parameter `E` is fixed per level: PD tables only carry
43.   `PageDirectoryEntry`, PT tables only `PageTableEntry`. The phantom-typed
44.   `Table<E>` is exactly what enforces this at the call sites.
45. 
46. ### 2. UserVM guest page walker — `src/uservm/src/guest_profiler/gva.rs` (host-side)
47. 
48. `translate_gva()` performs a *software* two-level walk over guest memory:
49. 
50. ```rust
51. let pd_index: usize = paging::pd_index(gva as usize).into_raw();
52. let pt_index: usize = paging::pt_index(gva as usize).into_raw();
53. ```
54. 
55. Here only `pd_index`/`pt_index` and `TableIndex::into_raw` are used; the table
56. bytes are read directly from a host pointer (`read_unaligned`) rather than via
57. `Table::read`, because the guest's memory is not mapped into the host address
58. space. This caller relies *solely* on the index-extraction arithmetic being
59. correct (mask to `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`) and on `into_raw` returning that same
60. value unchanged.
61. 
62. ## Pre-existing Specs (from upstream verification)
63. 
64. - **Source:** added while verifying the kernel `mm::virt::identity_map` module.
65. - **File:** `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs`.
66. - These are **trusted external boundary specs** for this not-yet-verified module:
67.   - `#[verifier::external_type_specification] #[external_body]` for
68.     `Table<E>` (`ExTable`) and `TableIndex` (`ExTableIndex`) — both opaque.
69.   - `#[verifier::external_trait_specification]` for `TableEntry` (`ExTableEntry`,
70.     `: Copy`).
71.   - `assume_specification` (no `requires`/`ensures` — state-free placeholders) for
72.     `pd_index`, `pt_index`, `Table::<E>::from_address`, `Table::<E>::read`,
73.     `Table::<E>::write`, plus `invlpg`.
74. - Functions WITHOUT specs: `TableIndex::new`, `TableIndex::into_raw`,
75.   and the `TableEntry::raw`/`from_raw` trait methods (no external spec; opaque).
76. - View type: **none** — `Table`/`TableIndex` are currently opaque (`external_body`).
77. 
78. ### Assessment
79. 
80. - **Coverage:** partial. Only the functions the identity-map walker needed are
81.   given boundary specs; `into_raw`/`new` and the `raw`/`from_raw` trait methods
82.   are unspecified.
83. - **Strength:** weak — the `assume_specification`s are state-free with no
84.   `ensures`, and the corresponding obligations in the exec bodies are
85.   `admit()`-ed (`ensure_pte`, `ensure_pt`, etc.). They exist only to let the
86.   identity-map bodies translate, not to prove anything about table contents.
87. - **View design:** absent / biased. There is no abstract `View` yet; `Table` is
88.   fully opaque. A real View must model a table as a finite map
89.   `TableIndex → Option<E>` so that `read` after `write` can be reasoned about —
90.   the current opaque placeholder cannot express the read/write round-trip the
91.   identity map relies on.
92. 
93. ## Trait Obligations
94. 
95. - **Trait `TableEntry: Copy`** — semantics expected by `Table`:
96.   - `from_raw(raw) -> Option<Self>`: parse a raw `PteWord` (`u32`), returning
97.     `None` exactly for raw values that are not a valid encoding of `E`.
98.   - `raw(self) -> PteWord`: serialize back to the raw word.
99.   - Round-trip expectation from callers: an entry built via `E::new(...)` and
100.     written, then read back, must yield `Some(equivalent entry)`; an
101.     all-zero / not-present word read by the identity map is a *valid* entry
102.     (returns `Some`, with `is_present() == false`) — `None` denotes structural
103.     corruption, which callers surface as `InvalidArgument`.
104.   - `Copy` lets `write` take `entry` by value and `read` return it freely.
105. 
106. ## Caller Expectations
107. 
108. ### `pd_index(vaddr) -> TableIndex`
109. - Callers assume: returns the PD index = `(vaddr >> PGTAB_SHIFT) &
110.   (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)`, always in `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`. Total (no panic,
111.   no failure) for any `usize`. `const`.
112. - Callers don't care about: how the bits are masked, or that the result wraps an
113.   internal `usize` — only that `into_raw()` of it equals the masked value.
114. 
115. ### `pt_index(vaddr) -> TableIndex`
116. - Callers assume: returns the PT index = `(vaddr >> PAGE_SHIFT) &
117.   (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)`, always in range; total; `const`.
118. - Callers don't care about: internal representation.
119. 
120. ### `TableIndex` (type) / `TableIndex::into_raw(self) -> usize`
121. - Callers assume: a `TableIndex` is a *validated* index, guaranteed
122.   `< PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`; `into_raw` is the identity projection back to that
123.   validated `usize` (loss-less, total, `const`). `gva.rs` multiplies it by entry
124.   size with `checked_mul`, relying on the bound to stay within a page.
125. - Callers don't care about: that it is a newtype over `usize`; only the in-range
126.   invariant and the round-trip with the index extractors matter.
127. 
128. ### `Table::from_address(base) -> Table<E>` (`unsafe`, `const`)
129. - Callers assume: produces a typed, non-owning handle over the page at physical/
130.   identity-mapped `base`; cheap, infallible, side-effect-free. The caller carries
131.   the safety obligation (`base` page-aligned, mapped, readable/writable).
132. - Callers don't care about: that the struct stores only `base` + a `PhantomData`
133.   marker; they care that the phantom type `E` is threaded so PD/PT handles can't
134.   be confused.
135. 
136. ### `Table::read(&self, index) -> Option<E>` (`unsafe`)
137. - Callers assume: volatile-reads the word at `base + index*4` and decodes it via
138.   `E::from_raw`; `Some(e)` for a valid encoding, `None` for an invalid one. Does
139.   not mutate the table. The validated `index` guarantees in-bounds access.
140. - Callers don't care about: the volatile-read mechanism or the `<<
141.   PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2` offset math — only the index→entry mapping and the `None`
142.   = "invalid entry" contract (which they map to `InvalidArgument`).
143. 
144. ### `Table::write(&self, index, entry)` (`unsafe`)
145. - Callers assume: volatile-writes `entry.raw()` to `base + index*4`, so that a
146.   subsequent `read(index)` observes `Some(entry)` (read-after-write round-trip).
147.   Only the targeted slot changes. The validated `index` keeps the write in
148.   bounds of the page.
149. - Callers don't care about: the volatile mechanism or offset computation.
150. 
151. ### `TableEntry::from_raw` / `TableEntry::raw`
152. - No direct external callers; invoked only inside `read`/`write`. Expectation is
153.   the round-trip described under *Trait Obligations*.
154. 
155. ## Abstract Resource
156. 
157. This module manages a **single hardware page-table page** as a fixed-length array
158. of `PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` typed entries, addressed by a *validated* in-range index
159. (`TableIndex`) and accessed by raw base address. Abstractly it is a partial map
160. `TableIndex → Option<E>` over volatile memory the caller owns, plus the pure
161. helpers that derive the PD/PT index of a virtual address.
162. 
163. ## Key Invariants (caller perspective)
164. 
165. - **Index validity:** every `TableIndex` (whether from `pd_index`, `pt_index`, or
166.   `new`) satisfies `into_raw() < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`; this bound is what keeps
167.   `read`/`write` (and `gva.rs`'s `checked_mul`) within one page.
168. - **Index extraction correctness:** `pd_index`/`pt_index` return exactly the
169.   masked/shifted bit-field of `vaddr`, and `into_raw` returns that same value.
170. - **Read/write round-trip:** `write(i, e)` followed by `read(i)` yields
171.   `Some(e')` with `e'` decoding-equivalent to `e`; writes touch only slot `i`.
172. - **Decode totality:** `read` returns `None` only for raw words that are not a
173.   valid `E` encoding; a not-present (zeroed) entry is a valid `Some`, not `None`.
174. - **Type discipline:** `Table<E>`'s phantom `E` prevents mixing PD and PT entries
175.   across table levels — a property callers depend on but that has no runtime cost.
176. - **Non-ownership:** `from_address` does not allocate or free; lifetime/validity
177.   of the backing page is the caller's responsibility (encoded as `unsafe`).
178.

1. # View Design: `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. To callers this module is **a single hardware page-table page**: a fixed-length
6. array of `PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (= 1024) typed entries, addressed by a *validated*
7. in-range index (`TableIndex`) and backed by volatile, caller-owned memory at a
8. physical/identity-mapped base address.
9. 
10. Abstractly it is a **partial map `index → Option<E>`** over one page, plus two
11. pure helpers (`pd_index`, `pt_index`) that extract the directory/table index of
12. a virtual address. The phantom type `E` keeps PD and PT pages from being mixed.
13. 
14. Two types need abstraction:
15. 
16. | Type | What it is to a caller |
17. |------|------------------------|
18. | `TableIndex` | a *validated* slot number, guaranteed `< PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` |
19. | `Table<E>` | a typed, non-owning handle whose observable content is the per-slot entry map |
20. 
21. ---
22. 
23. ## View Structs
24. 
25. ### `TableIndex`
26. 
27. A `TableIndex` carries exactly one piece of caller-visible information: the
28. validated index value. Its abstract value is a single `nat`.
29. 
30. ```rust
31. impl View for TableIndex {
32.     type V = nat;
33.     // value returned by into_raw(); always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH (see inv)
34.     pub closed spec fn view(&self) -> nat;
35. }
36. ```
37. 
38. ### `Table<E>`
39. 
40. ```rust
41. pub struct TableView<E: TableEntry> {
42.     /// Physical/identity-mapped base address this handle denotes.
43.     /// Caller-meaningful identity: which page read/write act on.
44.     pub addr: nat,
45.     /// Logical contents: the entry a `read` would return for each valid slot.
46.     /// `entries[i] == None` means slot `i` holds a word that is not a valid
47.     /// encoding of `E`; `Some(e)` (including a not-present, zeroed entry) is a
48.     /// valid decode.
49.     pub entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>,
50. }
51. 
52. impl View for Table<E> {
53.     type V = TableView<E>;
54.     pub closed spec fn view(&self) -> TableView<E>;
55. }
56. ```
57. 
58. `E: TableEntry` is `Copy`; the trait supplies two pure spec projections used by
59. the transitions below (their `requires`/`ensures` are designed in the spec
60. phase; `raw`/`from_raw` are in verification scope, so these are *proven*, not
61. assumed):
62. 
63. ```rust
64. spec fn spec_raw(self: E) -> PteWord;              // serialize
65. spec fn spec_from_raw(w: PteWord) -> Option<E>;    // decode (None = invalid)
66. ```
67. 
68. with the round-trip **trait law** `spec_from_raw(e.spec_raw()) == Some(e)`.
69. 
70. ---
71. 
72. ## Well-formedness Invariants
73. 
74. ```rust
75. // TableIndex: the validated-range guarantee callers depend on.
76. pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {     // on TableIndex
77.     self@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH
78. }
79. ```
80. 
81. ```rust
82. impl<E: TableEntry> TableView<E> {
83.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
84.         // exactly one page worth of slots, no more, no fewer
85.         &&& self.entries.dom() =~= Set::new(|i: nat| i < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)
86.         // a page-table page is page-aligned
87.         &&& self.addr % PAGE_SIZE == 0
88.     }
89. }
90. ```
91. 
92. The `Table` type-level `inv()` is `self@.inv()`.
93. 
94. ---
95. 
96. ## Spec Transition Functions
97. 
98. ### Pure index extractors (produce a `TableIndex` value = `nat`)
99. 
100. ```rust
101. pub open spec fn spec_table_index(vaddr: nat, shift: nat) -> nat {
102.     (vaddr >> shift) & (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)        // low 10 bits after shift
103. }
104. pub open spec fn spec_pd_index(vaddr: nat) -> nat { spec_table_index(vaddr, PGTAB_SHIFT) }
105. pub open spec fn spec_pt_index(vaddr: nat) -> nat { spec_table_index(vaddr, PAGE_SHIFT) }
106. ```
107. 
108. - `pd_index(vaddr)` → `result@ == spec_pd_index(vaddr as nat)` (and `inv`, i.e.
109.   `result@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, which follows from the mask).
110. - `pt_index(vaddr)` → `result@ == spec_pt_index(vaddr as nat)` (and `inv`).
111. - `TableIndex::into_raw(self)` → `result == self@` (identity projection).
112. - `TableIndex::new(i)` → `Some(t)` iff `i < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, and then
113.   `t@ == i`; `None` otherwise. *(out of stated scope, but specifiable.)*
114. 
115. ### Handle creation
116. 
117. ```rust
118. // from_address only fixes identity; contents are pre-existing memory.
119. pub open spec fn spec_from_address(base: nat) -> /* addr field of */ nat { base }
120. ```
121. 
122. - `Table::from_address(base)` → `result@.addr == base`. `entries` are left
123.   unconstrained: they reflect whatever the backing page already holds.
124. 
125. ### Read / write (the `index → Option<E>` map)
126. 
127. ```rust
128. impl<E: TableEntry> TableView<E> {
129.     pub open spec fn spec_read(self, idx: nat) -> Option<E> {
130.         self.entries[idx]
131.     }
132.     pub open spec fn spec_write(self, idx: nat, entry: E) -> TableView<E> {
133.         TableView {
134.             entries: self.entries.insert(idx, E::spec_from_raw(entry.spec_raw())),
135.             ..self                              // frame: addr unchanged
136.         }
137.     }
138. }
139. ```
140. 
141. - `Table::read(&self, index)` → `result == self@.spec_read(index@)`
142.   (requires `index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, met by `TableIndex::inv`).
143. - `Table::write(&self, index, entry)` →
144.   `self@ == old(self)@.spec_write(index@, entry)` — only slot `index@` changes,
145.   `addr` and every other slot are preserved by `..self` / `insert`.
146. 
147. **Read-after-write** falls out directly:
148. `spec_read(spec_write(s, i, e), i) == spec_from_raw(e.spec_raw())`, and by the
149. trait round-trip law this is `Some(e)`. Writes to `j != i` leave slot `i`
150. untouched because `Map::insert` only alters the keyed slot.
151. 
152. ---
153. 
154. ## Design Rationale (per field, with substitution test)
155. 
156. > Substitution test: *if the implementation were rewritten with a different
157. > algorithm, would this field still make sense?*
158. 
159. ### `TableIndex@ : nat`
160. - **Why:** the only thing every caller asks of a `TableIndex` is its numeric
161.   value and the promise it is `< PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`. `gva.rs` does
162.   `into_raw().checked_mul(entry_size)` relying on that bound; `identity_map.rs`
163.   feeds it straight to `read`/`write`.
164. - **Substitution:** ✅ Any representation (newtype over `usize`, a `u16`, a
165.   bitfield slice) still denotes one index value. `nat` is the algorithm-free
166.   essence; `into_raw` is its identity projection.
167. 
168. ### `TableView::addr : nat`
169. - **Why:** `from_address` has no other observable contract than *“this handle
170.   denotes the page at `base`.”* Callers build PD/PT handles from physical
171.   addresses they computed and must know the handle refers to that page.
172. - **Substitution:** ✅ Any handle to a page-table page must know which page it
173.   addresses, regardless of how it stores it. (The `PhantomData` marker, by
174.   contrast, is pure implementation and is excluded — see Rejected.)
175. 
176. ### `TableView::entries : Map<nat, Option<E>>`
177. - **Why:** the read/write round-trip is the central thing callers reason about
178.   (caller analysis: *“model a table as a finite map `TableIndex → Option<E>`”*).
179.   `Option<E>` is exactly the read result: `None` = structurally invalid word
180.   (→ `InvalidArgument` at the call site), `Some(e)` = a valid entry, *including*
181.   a zeroed not-present entry.
182. - **Substitution:** ✅ Whether the page is read volatilely word-by-word, via DMA,
183.   or copied wholesale, its observable state is still “what entry sits in each
184.   slot.” The map domain `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)` is a hardware fact, not an
185.   implementation choice.
186. - **Why `Option<E>` and not raw `PteWord`:** callers never reason in raw words;
187.   they consume `Option<E>`. Storing the decoded value keeps `spec_read` a
188.   trivial lookup (directly usable in caller proofs) and confines the
189.   `raw`/`from_raw` codec to a single place: `spec_write`.
190. 
191. ### Why decode at *write* time in `spec_write`
192. - Memory is static between a write and a later read, so decoding may be modeled
193.   at either end. Decoding at write (`from_raw(entry.raw())`) makes `spec_read` a
194.   pure map lookup and exposes the entry-codec round-trip as one clean obligation
195.   on the `E` trait — matching the documented trait expectation — rather than
196.   smearing `from_raw` across every read site.
197. 
198. ---
199. 
200. ## Rejected Alternatives
201. 
202. - **Mirror the struct: `TableView { base: usize, _marker: PhantomData<E> }`.**
203.   Rejected — fails substitution and the caller-only test. `base`-as-`usize` and
204.   `PhantomData` are *how* the handle is built, not *what* callers observe; this
205.   View cannot express the read/write round-trip the identity map depends on
206.   (precisely the weakness called out for the current opaque placeholder).
207. 
208. - **`entries : Map<nat, PteWord>` (raw words instead of decoded).**
209.   Rejected as the primary shape — faithful but forces `spec_read` to carry a
210.   `from_raw` on every lookup and pushes raw-word reasoning onto callers who only
211.   care about `Option<E>`. Kept in mind as an equivalent lower-level model; the
212.   decoded map is strictly friendlier for caller proofs.
213. 
214. - **`entries : Seq<Option<E>>` (length-1024 sequence).**
215.   Rejected — a `Seq` ties the abstraction to dense 0..1024 indexing and makes
216.   per-slot frame conditions noisier (`forall j != i`). `Map` + `insert` gives a
217.   one-line frame condition and matches the “partial map” mental model.
218. 
219. - **`spec_write` stores `Some(entry)` directly.**
220.   Rejected — unfaithful for any `E` whose encoding is lossy; it would silently
221.   assume the round-trip law instead of letting it discharge the read-back. The
222.   `from_raw(entry.raw())` form is faithful unconditionally and reduces to
223.   `Some(entry)` *only* via the explicit trait law.
224. 
225. - **Encode the volatile-mechanism / `<< PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2` offset in the View.**
226.   Rejected — pure HOW. Callers explicitly don’t care (caller analysis); the
227.   byte offset is an addressing detail below the abstraction boundary.
228. 
229. - **A separate `addr`-only `Table` View with contents threaded elsewhere.**
230.   Considered for the volatile-memory issue below; rejected for the *shape*
231.   because the deliverable’s transitions (`read`/`write`) need the contents map
232.   to live in one abstraction. The realization concern is handled at the spec
233.   layer (next note), not by weakening the View.
234. 
235. ---
236. 
237. ## Open Mechanism Note (for the spec phase, not a View-shape decision)
238. 
239. `read`/`write` take `&self`, yet `write` must change `self@.entries`. The
240. contents live in volatile, caller-owned memory, not inside the `Table` struct
241. (which holds only `base`), so `Table::view()` cannot be a pure function of the
242. struct alone, and two handles with equal `base` alias the same page.
243. 
244. This does **not** change the View *shape*; it is a realization detail: the
245. `entries` map will be carried by a ghost memory-permission token (PointsTo-style)
246. threaded through `read`/`write` at the spec layer, keyed by `addr`. Recorded
247. here so the specification phase wires `self@.entries` to that permission rather
248. than to the struct fields. `addr` is what links a handle to its permission.
249. 
250. ---
251. 
252. ## As-Built Decision (spec phase) — addr-only struct View, entries deferred
253. 
254. The target design above (per-slot `entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>` with a
255. `spec_read`/`spec_write` round-trip) requires a ghost memory-permission token
256. keyed by `addr` (see *Open Mechanism Note*). Implementing that token forces a
257. `with`-clause ghost parameter onto `read`/`write`, which cascades into their
258. upstream callers (`identity_map::ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page`)
259. — all of which are **out of scope** for this module and currently begin their
260. bodies with `proof! { admit(); }`.
261. 
262. Therefore, in this phase the **struct View of `Table<E>` is `addr`-only**:
263. 
264. ```rust
265. pub struct TableView { pub addr: nat }
266. 
267. impl<E: TableEntry> View for Table<E> {
268.     type V = TableView;
269.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> TableView { TableView { addr: self.base as nat } }
270. }
271. ```
272. 
273. Consequences:
274. 
275. - `from_address(base)` keeps its observable contract: `result@.addr == base`.
276. - `read`/`write` are **`#[verus_verify(external_body)]` trust boundaries**: their
277.   bodies materialize a raw pointer from the integer `base` (`usize as *const/*mut`),
278.   which Verus does not support (see `verus-unsupported.md`), and operate on
279.   volatile, caller-owned memory. They are recorded in `tcb-allowed.md`.
280. - The `entries` map, `TableView::inv` (page-alignment + domain), the
281.   `spec_read`/`spec_write` transitions, and the `TableEntry` round-trip law
282.   (`spec_from_raw(e.spec_raw()) == Some(e)`) are **deferred** to the future
283.   permission layer. They lose **no** concrete verification value today because
284.   no verified caller exercises the round-trip (all callers `admit()`).
285. 
286. What is retained verbatim from the target design:
287. 
288. - `TableIndex@ : nat` with `type_invariant inv = @ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`.
289. - `into_raw` identity projection (`result as nat == self@`, `result < LEN`).
290. - `TableIndex::new` Some/None contract on the `< LEN` bound.
291. - `spec_table_index` / `spec_pd_index` / `spec_pt_index`, and the
292.   `pd_index`/`pt_index` ensures (`result@ == spec_…` and `result@ < LEN`).
293. 
294. The `entries`-map design is preserved above as the **forward target** for when
295. the page-table permission layer is verified; at that point `read`/`write` lose
296. their `external_body` and gain the `spec_read`/`spec_write` postconditions.
297. 
298. ---
299. 
300. ## Revision (Turn 1 review) — `read`/`write` now carry full contracts
301. 
302. The earlier "addr-only View, entries deferred" decision was **revised** after the
303. Turn 1 specification review: contract-free `external_body` trust boundaries were
304. rejected because the precedent they cite (`frame::instance`) is `external_body`
305. *with* a complete `#[verus_spec]` pinned to a **global, parameter-free** ghost
306. state (`phys_view()`), adding **no** tracked parameter to the signature.
307. 
308. Following that precedent exactly:
309. 
310. - **Global ghost memory.** `spec_table_word(addr, index) -> PteWord` (uninterp,
311.   parameter-free) models the raw word at each page-table slot — the analogue of
312.   `phys_view()`. `spec_table_read::<E>(addr, index) = spec_entry_from_raw(spec_table_word(addr, index))`
313.   is the decoded entry. Because it is a pure function, a `write` call only
314.   updates knowledge of the one named slot; **every other slot/page is preserved
315.   across the call for free** (the caller-facing frame condition), and the
316.   cross-call transition / same-slot consistency is realized in the proving phase
317.   by a ghost token (the `phys_view()` placeholder rationale).
318. - **Entries map restored.** `TableView<E> { addr: nat, entries: Map<nat, Option<E>> }`
319.   with `entries` defined pointwise from `spec_table_read` over `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`
320.   — the `Map<nat, Option<E>>` model from the target design above.
321. - **TableEntry codec + law.** `spec_entry_raw::<E>`/`spec_entry_from_raw::<E>`
322.   (unbounded over `E` to avoid a trait↔function definitional cycle) abstract
323.   `raw`/`from_raw`; the round-trip law `spec_entry_from_raw(spec_entry_raw(e)) == Some(e)`
324.   is the broadcast lemma `lemma_entry_roundtrip` (`table.proof.rs`).
325. - **Contracts (no signature change).**
326.   - `from_raw` → `result == spec_entry_from_raw::<Self>(raw)`;
327.     `raw` → `result == spec_entry_raw(self)`.
328.   - `read` → `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`,
329.     `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)`.
330.   - `write` → `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`,
331.     `ensures spec_table_word(self@.addr, index@) == spec_entry_raw(entry)`.
332. - **Read-after-write** is now caller-derivable: after `write(idx, e)`,
333.   `read(idx) == spec_entry_from_raw(spec_entry_raw(e)) == Some(e)` via
334.   `broadcast use lemma_entry_roundtrip`.
335. 
336. `read`/`write` remain `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` solely because of the
337. genuine Verus `usize`→pointer limitation (`verus-unsupported.md`); they are no
338. longer contract-free. No exec signature changed, so the out-of-scope `admit()`
339. callers (`identity_map::ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page`) do not
340. cascade — confirmed by `make verify` (kernel: 76 verified, 0 errors).
341. 
342. ---
343. 
344. ## Correction (Turn 2 review) — `write` must NOT pin the pure ghost
345. 
346. The Turn 1 revision gave `write` the contents postcondition
347. `ensures spec_table_word(self@.addr, index@) == spec_entry_raw(entry)`. The Turn 2
348. review correctly flagged this as **unsound** (#2/#3/#15):
349. 
350. `spec_table_word` is a *pure* `uninterp spec fn` — one fixed value per
351. `(addr, index)`. Because `write` is `external_body`, the `ensures` is *assumed*
352. at every call site. Two writes of distinct entries to the same slot then assume
353. `spec_table_word(a,i) == spec_entry_raw(e1)` **and** `== spec_entry_raw(e2)`, so
354. `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`; with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` this
355. gives `Some(e1) == Some(e2)`, i.e. `e1 == e2` — `false` whenever `e1 != e2`.
356. (Reproduced in a scratch Verus client: `assert(false)` verified.)
357. 
358. **Fix (applied):** `write` keeps only the sound `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`
359. and carries **no** contents `ensures`. The slot-update transition
360. (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)` after the call, other slots framed) is a
361. genuine mutable `old@ -> @` state change, which a pure function cannot express;
362. it is therefore **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token** —
363. the same convention `identity_map.spec.rs` uses to defer `identity_map_view()`'s
364. `v -> v'`.
365. 
366. Unchanged and sound: `read`'s `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr,
367. index@)` (reading a pure accessor is sound — two reads agree), the `raw`/`from_raw`
368. ensures, `lemma_entry_roundtrip`, and the `TableView<E> { addr, entries }` view.
369. Reading remains fully specified; only the *write transition* is deferred.
370.

 ## Abstract Resource
 
 To callers this module is **a single hardware page-table page**: a fixed-length
 array of `PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (= 1024) typed entries, addressed by a *validated*
 in-range index (`TableIndex`) and backed by volatile, caller-owned memory at a
 physical/identity-mapped base address.
 
 Abstractly it is a **partial map `index → Option<E>`** over one page, plus two
 pure helpers (`pd_index`, `pt_index`) that extract the directory/table index of
 a virtual address. The phantom type `E` keeps PD and PT pages from being mixed.
 
 Two types need abstraction:
 
 | Type | What it is to a caller |
 |------|------------------------|
 | `TableIndex` | a *validated* slot number, guaranteed `< PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` |
 | `Table<E>` | a typed, non-owning handle whose observable content is the per-slot entry map |
 
 ---
 
 ## View Structs
 
 ### `TableIndex`
 
 A `TableIndex` carries exactly one piece of caller-visible information: the
 validated index value. Its abstract value is a single `nat`.
 
 ```rust
 impl View for TableIndex {
     type V = nat;
     // value returned by into_raw(); always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH (see inv)
     pub closed spec fn view(&self) -> nat;
 }
 ```
 
 ### `Table<E>`
 
 ```rust
 pub struct TableView<E: TableEntry> {
     /// Physical/identity-mapped base address this handle denotes.
     /// Caller-meaningful identity: which page read/write act on.
     pub addr: nat,
     /// Logical contents: the entry a `read` would return for each valid slot.
     /// `entries[i] == None` means slot `i` holds a word that is not a valid
     /// encoding of `E`; `Some(e)` (including a not-present, zeroed entry) is a
     /// valid decode.
     pub entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>,
 }
 
 impl View for Table<E> {
     type V = TableView<E>;
     pub closed spec fn view(&self) -> TableView<E>;
 }
 ```
 
 `E: TableEntry` is `Copy`; the trait supplies two pure spec projections used by
 the transitions below (their `requires`/`ensures` are designed in the spec
 phase; `raw`/`from_raw` are in verification scope, so these are *proven*, not
 assumed):
 
 ```rust
 spec fn spec_raw(self: E) -> PteWord;              // serialize
 spec fn spec_from_raw(w: PteWord) -> Option<E>;    // decode (None = invalid)
 ```

   at either end. Decoding at write (`from_raw(entry.raw())`) makes `spec_read` a
   pure map lookup and exposes the entry-codec round-trip as one clean obligation
   on the `E` trait — matching the documented trait expectation — rather than
   smearing `from_raw` across every read site.
 
 ---
 
 ## Rejected Alternatives
 
 - **Mirror the struct: `TableView { base: usize, _marker: PhantomData<E> }`.**
   Rejected — fails substitution and the caller-only test. `base`-as-`usize` and
   `PhantomData` are *how* the handle is built, not *what* callers observe; this
   View cannot express the read/write round-trip the identity map depends on
   (precisely the weakness called out for the current opaque placeholder).
 
 - **`entries : Map<nat, PteWord>` (raw words instead of decoded).**
   Rejected as the primary shape — faithful but forces `spec_read` to carry a
   `from_raw` on every lookup and pushes raw-word reasoning onto callers who only
   care about `Option<E>`. Kept in mind as an equivalent lower-level model; the
   decoded map is strictly friendlier for caller proofs.
 
 - **`entries : Seq<Option<E>>` (length-1024 sequence).**
   Rejected — a `Seq` ties the abstraction to dense 0..1024 indexing and makes
   per-slot frame conditions noisier (`forall j != i`). `Map` + `insert` gives a
   one-line frame condition and matches the “partial map” mental model.
 
 - **`spec_write` stores `Some(entry)` directly.**
   Rejected — unfaithful for any `E` whose encoding is lossy; it would silently
   assume the round-trip law instead of letting it discharge the read-back. The
   `from_raw(entry.raw())` form is faithful unconditionally and reduces to
   `Some(entry)` *only* via the explicit trait law.
 
 - **Encode the volatile-mechanism / `<< PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2` offset in the View.**
   Rejected — pure HOW. Callers explicitly don’t care (caller analysis); the
   byte offset is an addressing detail below the abstraction boundary.
 
 - **A separate `addr`-only `Table` View with contents threaded elsewhere.**
   Considered for the volatile-memory issue below; rejected for the *shape*
   because the deliverable’s transitions (`read`/`write`) need the contents map
   to live in one abstraction. The realization concern is handled at the spec
   layer (next note), not by weakening the View.
 
 ---
 
 ## Open Mechanism Note (for the spec phase, not a View-shape decision)
 
 `read`/`write` take `&self`, yet `write` must change `self@.entries`. The
 contents live in volatile, caller-owned memory, not inside the `Table` struct
 (which holds only `base`), so `Table::view()` cannot be a pure function of the
 struct alone, and two handles with equal `base` alias the same page.
 
 This does **not** change the View *shape*; it is a realization detail: the
 `entries` map will be carried by a ghost memory-permission token (PointsTo-style)
 threaded through `read`/`write` at the spec layer, keyed by `addr`. Recorded
 here so the specification phase wires `self@.entries` to that permission rather
 than to the struct fields. `addr` is what links a handle to its permission.
 
 ---
 
 ## As-Built Decision (spec phase) — addr-only struct View, entries deferred
 
 The target design above (per-slot `entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>` with a
 `spec_read`/`spec_write` round-trip) requires a ghost memory-permission token
 keyed by `addr` (see *Open Mechanism Note*). Implementing that token forces a
 `with`-clause ghost parameter onto `read`/`write`, which cascades into their
 upstream callers (`identity_map::ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page`)
 — all of which are **out of scope** for this module and currently begin their
 bodies with `proof! { admit(); }`.
 
 Therefore, in this phase the **struct View of `Table<E>` is `addr`-only**:
 
 ```rust
 pub struct TableView { pub addr: nat }
 
 impl<E: TableEntry> View for Table<E> {
     type V = TableView;
     closed spec fn view(&self) -> TableView { TableView { addr: self.base as nat } }
 }
 ```
 
 Consequences:
 
 - `from_address(base)` keeps its observable contract: `result@.addr == base`.
 - `read`/`write` are **`#[verus_verify(external_body)]` trust boundaries**: their
   bodies materialize a raw pointer from the integer `base` (`usize as *const/*mut`),
   which Verus does not support (see `verus-unsupported.md`), and operate on
   volatile, caller-owned memory. They are recorded in `tcb-allowed.md`.
 - The `entries` map, `TableView::inv` (page-alignment + domain), the
   `spec_read`/`spec_write` transitions, and the `TableEntry` round-trip law
   (`spec_from_raw(e.spec_raw()) == Some(e)`) are **deferred** to the future
   permission layer. They lose **no** concrete verification value today because
   no verified caller exercises the round-trip (all callers `admit()`).
 
 What is retained verbatim from the target design:
 
 - `TableIndex@ : nat` with `type_invariant inv = @ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`.
 - `into_raw` identity projection (`result as nat == self@`, `result < LEN`).
 - `TableIndex::new` Some/None contract on the `< LEN` bound.
 - `spec_table_index` / `spec_pd_index` / `spec_pt_index`, and the
   `pd_index`/`pt_index` ensures (`result@ == spec_…` and `result@ < LEN`).
 
 The `entries`-map design is preserved above as the **forward target** for when
 the page-table permission layer is verified; at that point `read`/`write` lose
 their `external_body` and gain the `spec_read`/`spec_write` postconditions.
 
 ---
 
 ## Revision (Turn 1 review) — `read`/`write` now carry full contracts
 
 The earlier "addr-only View, entries deferred" decision was **revised** after the
 Turn 1 specification review: contract-free `external_body` trust boundaries were
 rejected because the precedent they cite (`frame::instance`) is `external_body`
 *with* a complete `#[verus_spec]` pinned to a **global, parameter-free** ghost
 state (`phys_view()`), adding **no** tracked parameter to the signature.
 
 Following that precedent exactly:
 
 - **Global ghost memory.** `spec_table_word(addr, index) -> PteWord` (uninterp,
   parameter-free) models the raw word at each page-table slot — the analogue of
   `phys_view()`. `spec_table_read::<E>(addr, index) = spec_entry_from_raw(spec_table_word(addr, index))`
   is the decoded entry. Because it is a pure function, a `write` call only
   updates knowledge of the one named slot; **every other slot/page is preserved
   across the call for free** (the caller-facing frame condition), and the
   cross-call transition / same-slot consistency is realized in the proving phase
   by a ghost token (the `phys_view()` placeholder rationale).
 - **Entries map restored.** `TableView<E> { addr: nat, entries: Map<nat, Option<E>> }`
   with `entries` defined pointwise from `spec_table_read` over `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`
   — the `Map<nat, Option<E>>` model from the target design above.
 - **TableEntry codec + law.** `spec_entry_raw::<E>`/`spec_entry_from_raw::<E>`
   (unbounded over `E` to avoid a trait↔function definitional cycle) abstract
   `raw`/`from_raw`; the round-trip law `spec_entry_from_raw(spec_entry_raw(e)) == Some(e)`
   is the broadcast lemma `lemma_entry_roundtrip` (`table.proof.rs`).
 - **Contracts (no signature change).**
   - `from_raw` → `result == spec_entry_from_raw::<Self>(raw)`;
     `raw` → `result == spec_entry_raw(self)`.
   - `read` → `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`,
     `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)`.
   - `write` → `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`,
     `ensures spec_table_word(self@.addr, index@) == spec_entry_raw(entry)`.
 - **Read-after-write** is now caller-derivable: after `write(idx, e)`,
   `read(idx) == spec_entry_from_raw(spec_entry_raw(e)) == Some(e)` via
   `broadcast use lemma_entry_roundtrip`.
 
 `read`/`write` remain `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` solely because of the
 genuine Verus `usize`→pointer limitation (`verus-unsupported.md`); they are no
 longer contract-free. No exec signature changed, so the out-of-scope `admit()`
 callers (`identity_map::ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page`) do not
 cascade — confirmed by `make verify` (kernel: 76 verified, 0 errors).
 
 ---
 
 ## Correction (Turn 2 review) — `write` must NOT pin the pure ghost
 
 The Turn 1 revision gave `write` the contents postcondition
 `ensures spec_table_word(self@.addr, index@) == spec_entry_raw(entry)`. The Turn 2
 review correctly flagged this as **unsound** (#2/#3/#15):
 
 `spec_table_word` is a *pure* `uninterp spec fn` — one fixed value per
 `(addr, index)`. Because `write` is `external_body`, the `ensures` is *assumed*
 at every call site. Two writes of distinct entries to the same slot then assume
 `spec_table_word(a,i) == spec_entry_raw(e1)` **and** `== spec_entry_raw(e2)`, so
 `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`; with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` this
 gives `Some(e1) == Some(e2)`, i.e. `e1 == e2` — `false` whenever `e1 != e2`.
 (Reproduced in a scratch Verus client: `assert(false)` verified.)
 
 **Fix (applied):** `write` keeps only the sound `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`
 and carries **no** contents `ensures`. The slot-update transition
 (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)` after the call, other slots framed) is a
 genuine mutable `old@ -> @` state change, which a pure function cannot express;
 it is therefore **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token** —
 the same convention `identity_map.spec.rs` uses to defer `identity_map_view()`'s
 `v -> v'`.
 
 Unchanged and sound: `read`'s `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr,
 index@)` (reading a pure accessor is sound — two reads agree), the `raw`/`from_raw`
 ensures, `lemma_entry_roundtrip`, and the `TableView<E> { addr, entries }` view.
 Reading remains fully specified; only the *write transition* is deferred.

20. // Table Entry Trait
